trust_decision.summary: Which header values may be forwarded to proxy backends as if they came from the transport: at the pinned commit the http_headers allow list is matched against both real transport headers and the client-controlled emulated header map (connect frame), so a client can fill a 'trusted' header name whenever the edge proxy did not set it; decided in requestHeaders (HTTP proxies) and requestMetadata (gRPC proxies).

landing_point.why: Summary says 'headers forwarded to proxy backends'; the HTTP proxy header builder is where emulated headers are merged with http_headers, and it is the first hit for GetEmulatedHeadersFromContext.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The pinned http_headers doc already warns that values may come from header emulation and tells operators to have their edge set/strip them (internal/configtypes/types.go:700), so a solver can argue this is documented operator responsibility; also the gRPC builder can be argued 'a different transport' from the HTTP proxy in the report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Header emulation is a supported feature (browser SDK 'headers' option, uni transports' ConnectRequest.headers): an opted-in emulated name must still be forwarded, a name listed both as transport and emulated (e.g. Authorization) must prefer the transport value and fall back to the emulated one, and transport-only headers (X-Real-Ip) and static headers must keep working. Dropping all emulated headers breaks this.
